source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
description: The Round Leaf Peperomia is a creeping, semi-succulent, herbaceous perennial and an epiphyte that is native to Central and South America. Its trailing and creeping habit and peculiar round leaves make it great for hanging baskets. The leaves are bright green, small, round, and plump. This plant is ideal as a houseplant or office plant due to its easy care and compact size. The plant prefers bright, indirect sunlight and moist, well-drained soil. Avoid cold drafts and direct sunlight. The plant thrives in high humidity, but it is tolerant of normal household conditions. Consider using a humidifier or setting in the plant container on a tray of wet pebbles to increase the interior humidity. Quick ID Hints: creeping, semi-succulent, epiphyte, trailing habit, up to 12 inches long slender, fleshy, brownish stems with fine hairs thick, round, soft, bright green leaves with light green veins flowers are small yellowish spikes Insects, Diseases, and Other Plant Problems: Monitor for mealybugs. It may be susceptible to root rot, cutting rot, and ring spots. Curling leaves may result from low humidity or dry soil. Yellow leaves result from overwatering. More information on Peperomia .

cultivars.name: Hope
cultivars.note: low growing, trailing habit with miniature green round leaves, slow growing

Distribution: Argentina, Belize, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Puerto Rico, Suriname, Trinidad-Tobago, and Venezuela
Light: Dappled Sunlight (Shade through upper canopy all day)
Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)
Flower Description: The flowers are short yellowish spikes. Indoor plants rarely flower.
Leaf Description: Bright green, thick rounded leaves, and less than 0.5 inches in diameter.
Stem Description: Slender, fleshy, brownish stems with tiny fine hairs.
